- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < 0.33) and supply net is large negative, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots and fails to revert — apply mean reversion bias toward prior 5-10 day average if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- In high-event periods (e.g., >15 events/30d, net supply negative), model underestimates downside risk — increase downward bias by 5-10% of recent volatility if sentiment is bearish.
- If sentiment is bullish but price history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3-5 consecutive days above 65), model may overestimate continuation — reduce forecast slope or add downward drag.
- In low-event periods (e.g., <10 events), model often fails to capture sentiment shifts — adjust forecast based on sentiment history lag (e.g., if sentiment drops after 3 days, reduce forecast by 2-3% per day).
- When supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model tends to ignore supply shock — add downward adjustment proportional to supply net magnitude (e.g., -0.1 * supply_net for 30d forecast).
